newsitem.title: USA: Shuffle Master converts game to new format.
newsitem.headline: Shuffle Master converts game to new format.

text.p: Shuffle Master Inc said Monday it planned to convert its "The Tournament" version of "Let It Ride" game to a new bonus format with a fixed fee, and the change was expected to have "minimal impact" on profits this year.

The new bonus version will be marketed with a fixed monthly fee pricing structure not connected to casino revenue from the game. The company said it would no longer offer any tournaments where it shared in game revenues and managed playoffs.

While the new format was expected to produce lower revenue, it was expected to be offset by cost savings from the discontinued tournament operations, the company said. Profit contribution from the Let It Ride Bonus game was expected to grow as new tables were added, especially in fiscal year 1998.
In addition, Shuffle Master said it completed a test of its new video poker game Five Deck Frenzy and planned to begin rolling the product out to Nevada casinos immediately.
Mark Yoseloff, the game's inventor and executive vice president of Shuffle Master, said it was too early to project the number of installations.
"We have had inquiries from casinos in other markets and will evaluate those opportunities in the near future," he said in a statement.
